🇲🇽🇨🇺 <u>"THE ISLAND WILL NOT SURRENDER": CUBA'S EMBASSY IN MEXICO MARKS FIDEL'S CENTENARY</u>

At the Mexico presentation of "Fidel: 17 aproximaciones," coordinated by John Saxe-Fernández, Cuba's second chief of mission Johana Tablada put it plainly: "Though it hurts imperialism, the Cuban people still follow the example of resistance and rebellion marked by Fidel Castro." Blackouts of over 20 hours, shortages of water and medicine — a US blockade built to collapse the island. A century after Fidel's birth, Havana's answer is the same: no se rinde.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>MEXICO'S TAX AUTHORITY TURNS ON ITS OWN: 74 OFFICIALS REPORTED TO PROSECUTORS</u>

The cleanup starts at home. Mexico's SAT has denounced 74 of its own officials before the FGR so far this year — the highest figure in two decades. Hacienda's breakdown: 34 for illicit access to the agency's own computer systems, 28 for abuse of their powers. While the old guard screams "persecution," the 4T is auditing the people who collect the taxes.

text: ‍REUTERS: Mexico central bank holds rate at 6.5%, delays inflation target return August 6, 2026 | 🟢 📰 Reuters ran the Banxico decision straight: benchmark rate stays at 6.5%, convergence to the 3% target now expected in late 2027. No editorializing. 🇲🇽 The fuller picture: July CPI printed 3.12% — a five-year low — and Q2 GDP grew 6.1% annualized after the first-quarter contraction, with exports up 20% year-on-year through June.

‍EL PAÍS: Mexico reinforces ties with Brazil amid escalating tension between Lula and Trump August 7, 2026 | 🟡 📰 EL PAÍS covers the Mexico-Brazil binational commission as a last stand: two "progressive strongholds" huddling against "the Anglosphere." The actual news — Pemex-Petrobras joint oil exploration in the Gulf, $13.9B in bilateral trade, a shared UN bid for Bachelet — sits inside a eulogy for the region's left. 🇲🇽🇧🇷 • "the main bulwark against interventionist ambitions coming from the Anglosphere" • "the last lifeline for progressives facing the region's rightward shift" • "Sheinbaum does not want to provoke Trump any further"

text:
🇲🇽🏭 <u>US TRADE PRESSURE BITES: AUTO EXPORTS FALL 9.7% IN JULY</u>

Mexico's light-vehicle exports dropped 9.69% in July and production fell 2.2%, INEGI data shows, as trade tensions with Washington and T-MEC uncertainty hit the industry's most US-dependent sector. Year-to-date exports hold at 1.95 million vehicles, just 0.26% below 2025.

The strongest argument yet for what Mexico is already doing: diversifying markets so no single buyer can weaponize access.

🇲🇽🛒 <u>SUPERISSSTE RISES FROM THE NEOLIBERAL GRAVEYARD</u>

The state store chain decades of austerity left to rot just posted a 206% increase in sales compared to 2024.

ISSSTE director Martí Batres announced new SUPERISSSTE stores and expanded products to support workers' families — part of the Second Floor of the Fourth Transformation. What neoliberalism gutted, the 4T is rebuilding, store by store.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>SHEINBAUM TO SALAZAR: THE MAYO ZAMBADA TRANSFER IS NOT "WATER UNDER THE BRIDGE"</u>

Ex-ambassador Ken Salazar wants Mexico to "leave behind" the illegal transfer of Ismael Mayo Zambada to the United States. The President's answer:

"When there is interference by a country — in particular the United States toward Mexico, or probable interference — it's not a matter of saying: well, it's over, nothing happened." For the people of Mexico, she added, it is indispensable that everything be clarified.

A violation of sovereignty doesn't expire.

🇲🇽🎓 <u>THE REAL UNAM CHEATS AREN'T THE STUDENTS</u>

Contralínea asks the question the headline-hunters won't touch: who are the real cheaters at UNAM?

Not the kids who gamed an online exam — but the meritocracy narrative itself, when the admission exam works as an instrument of exclusion; the rector and university elites who are the exam's real deciders; a full-time faculty hiring system rigged by dedazos; and an antidemocratic university government.

The scandal was never about 3,200 exams. It's about who the exam is designed to keep out.
